title: Best Hourly Employee Time Tracking Software in 2026
summary: Compare the best hourly employee time tracking software for small teams, with pricing and user reviews.
body_markdown:
On Sunday night, a manager adds up handwritten punches and texted “I got in at 8” messages. The schedule said 38 hours. Every early arrival and late finish pushes the week to 41, and that last hour now costs time and a half.


Hourly employee time tracking software fixes that by recording every clock-in and clock-out as it happens, flagging overtime before it lands, and sending clean hours to payroll. The right pick depends on how your team clocks in, whether you need GPS, and what the bill looks like at 10 or 25 employees.


This guide compares seven apps that work as a time tracking app for small business hourly teams. You’ll see real pricing, what the free plans cover, and what owners say after months of daily use.


## **Best Hourly Employee Time Tracking Software: Quick Picks**


The best hourly employee time tracking software comes down to team size and how people clock in. The best time tracking software for small business owners is the one that fits both. All seven picks, ranked:


1. **Homebase:** time clock, timesheets, and payroll in one app, free for up to 10 employees.
2. **Clockify:** a free timer for teams of five or fewer.
3. **Jibble:** free for unlimited users, with face recognition and GPS.
4. **QuickBooks Time:** the natural fit if QuickBooks Online runs your books.
5. **Deputy:** a time clock plus scheduling for multi-location shifts.
6. **When I Work:** scheduling first, with a time clock you switch on per plan.
7. **Time Clock Wizard:** flat-rate pricing with unlimited users on the Value plan.


### Know your labor costs in real time.

## **Why Trust Homebase? Why We Built This Guide to Time Tracking for Hourly Employees**


A free app that changes its rules mid-year. A base fee that never appears on the pricing card. A GPS setting employees can switch off after they clock in. Those are the details that decide whether an app works for an hourly team, and they’re easy to miss on a pricing page.


Our app, Homebase, handles scheduling, a time clock and timesheets, payroll, hiring, and team communication for small businesses with hourly teams. You should know that before you read on: we publish this guide, Homebase is one of the seven apps in it, and every app was judged on its own merits. We never accept payment or backlinks for a mention.


We see how hourly teams clock in every day, because[more than 2 million hourly employees at over 150,000 small businesses](https://www.joinhomebase.com/data/september-2026-main-street-health-report) track their hours in Homebase. That’s why this guide cares about missed punches, paid breaks, and what happens when a phone loses signal at the edge of a job site, not only about price.


## **How We Chose the Best Employee Time Tracking Software**


Each app was scored on the things that go wrong on a real hourly team:


- How people clock in: phone, shared tablet, PIN, or photo.
- Whether GPS clock-in is free or paid.
- How overtime and breaks are handled.
- What happens when someone misses a punch.
- Approvals and edit history.
- The hand-off to payroll.
- Total monthly cost at 10 and 25 employees.


Pricing comes from each tool’s own pricing page. Ratings and quotes come from G2 and Capterra reviews, with patterns across reviews weighted over any single story. A Reddit thread of owners comparing clock-in apps helped test the criteria, and the cost totals are our own math from each tool’s listed monthly price.


That’s how we picked the best hourly employee time tracking software for small business teams. Our[full methodology](https://www.joinhomebase.com/methodology) shows how we evaluate every app we review, including the best time clock app for small business picks in our other guides.


Seven criteria across seven apps is a lot to keep straight, and no spreadsheet tells you what a missed punch looks like at 9am on a Saturday. One week on your real team answers most of it before payday does (our own[Homebase time clock](https://www.joinhomebase.com/time-clock) makes a pretty good guinea pig).

## **7 Best Time Tracking Software for Small Business Hourly Teams in 2026**


### **1. Homebase: best free time clock app for hourly teams.**


One login covers the time clock, timesheets, scheduling, and payroll, and the price is per location, not per user. That matters when a team grows, because a 10-person crew and a 30-person crew pay the same $30 for Essentials. The free Basic plan covers one location and up to 10 employees.


**Best for:** Hourly teams that want time clock, timesheets, scheduling, and payroll in one app.


**Rating:**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/homebase/reviews) 4.6 ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/153076/Homebase/reviews/) 4.6


**What it is:** A free-to-start time tracking app for hourly employees. Employees clock in on a shared tablet, computer, or POS device, or from their phones with the mobile time clock, and hours flow into timesheets and payroll.


**Key capabilities:**


- PINs on shared tablets, so every punch has a name on it.
- Location-based clock-in and photo capture on Essentials and up.
- Overtime alerts, early clock-in blocking, and automatic clock-out.
- Multiple wage rates for employees who work more than one role.
- Timesheets that feed payroll, with edit history on location-verified time cards.


**Pricing:** Free Basic plan for one location and up to 10 employees. Essentials is $30 per location per month with unlimited employees, and payroll adds $49 per month plus $6 per employee paid.


**What users like:** A[Capterra reviewer](https://capterra.com/p/153076/Homebase/reviews/?page=3) says the time clock is “free for the features that I need which is their time clock app,” and that it takes a picture of the person signing in. An owner at Ruru Baked sums up the mobile side:


“They can just have the \[Homebase\] app on their phone and sign in from anywhere — and I can see where they’re signing in from.”


Luanne Ronquillo, owner and founder of[Ruru Baked](https://www.joinhomebase.com/customers/ruru-baked-case-study-scheduling)


**What users criticize:** Another reviewer on the same[Capterra page](https://capterra.com/p/153076/Homebase/reviews/?page=3) reports that “location access was not always accurate” and that hours were easy for employees to falsely modify, though customer support eventually helped.


**Our take:** The free plan stops at 10 employees and one location, and GPS clock-in and photo capture are paid. If your team is bigger, or you need to verify where people clock in, plan on Essentials, which stays a flat $30 per location.


Know who clocked in, and where, before you approve a single timesheet. A location stamp on phone clock-ins and a photo on tablet and POS clock-ins give you that, along with overtime alerts, early clock-in blocking, and automatic clock-out. Start a 14-day trial of the[Homebase GPS time clock](https://www.joinhomebase.com/time-clock/mobile-gps-time-clock) and see it on your own team today.


### **2. Clockify: best free time tracking app for teams of five.**


Clockify built its name on a free plan with unlimited users, and that ended this year. The free plan now stops at five users, with reports limited to one month and PDF-only exports. For a team of five or fewer that needs a timer and basic timesheets, it still works. Larger hourly teams pay per seat.


**Best for:** Solo operators and teams of up to five who need a free timer and basic timesheets.


**Rating:**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/clockify/reviews) 4.5 ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/169607/Clockify/reviews/) 4.8


**What it is:** A timer and timesheet app that started with freelancers and now works as an employee hours tracker for small teams. Visit[Clockify](https://clockify.me/#nofollow) to see the plans.


**Key capabilities:**


- Timer and manual time entry on web, desktop, and mobile.
- Kiosk mode for a shared device on Basic and up.
- Time approval, an attendance and overtime report, and time rounding on Standard and up.
- QuickBooks integration on Standard and up.
- GPS tracking on Pro.


**Pricing:** Free for up to five users. Basic is $4.99, Standard is $6.99, and Pro is $9.99 per user per month.


**What users like:** “You get a lot with the free plan of Clockify,” writes one[Capterra reviewer](https://www.capterra.com/p/169607/Clockify/reviews/) , pointing to time tracked against specific tasks and projects.


**What users criticize:** Another reviewer says Clockify’s[mobile app](https://www.capterra.com/p/169607/Clockify/reviews/) “has not been the best,” with limited functionality and sync problems.


**Our take:** For an hourly team, the seat math decides it. Past five people you’re paying at least $4.99 per user, and approvals and overtime reporting don’t arrive until Standard at $6.99. GPS is another step up to Pro. Clockify suits solo operators and tiny crews best.


### **3. Jibble: free GPS time clock app with facial recognition.**


Jibble is free for unlimited users, and its homepage lists face recognition, selfie capture, GPS stamps, geofencing, a shared kiosk, and offline mode. That’s a long list for a $0 price, which makes it a strong starting point for a team that wants identity checks at clock-in without a monthly bill.


**Best for:** Teams that want a free hourly time tracker with identity checks.


**Rating:**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/jibble/reviews) 4.5 ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/156992/Jibble/reviews/) 4.8


**What it is:** A time and attendance app built for deskless teams, with timers, timesheets, approvals, and time off alongside the clock-in tools. You can see the full list on the[Jibble](https://www.jibble.io/#nofollow) site.


**Key capabilities:**


- Face recognition and selfie capture to verify who’s clocking in.
- GPS stamps and geofencing to restrict clock-ins to approved locations, with more geofences on paid plans.
- NFC and PIN options for a shared kiosk.
- Offline mode that syncs once the device reconnects.
- Timesheet approvals and XLS or CSV exports.


**Pricing:** Free for unlimited users. Paid plans add group management, custom break and overtime rules, and more geofences and kiosks.


**What users like:** A reviewer on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/jibble/reviews) says the “facial recognition feature on the shared tablet scans fast” and logs the timestamp right away.


**What users criticize:** Another G2 reviewer notes that Jibble[“automatically marks all break time as unpaid,”](https://www.g2.com/products/jibble/reviews) so her manager adds the paid half hour by hand.


**Our take:** Free is hard to beat, so test the break rules before you commit. Custom break and overtime rules sit on paid plans, so a team with paid breaks should confirm the settings match your policy before payday does the testing for you.


### **4. QuickBooks Time: employee time tracking app for QuickBooks users.**


QuickBooks Time earns its place if QuickBooks Online already runs your books, because hours sync straight into payroll and invoicing. The price has two parts: a monthly base fee and a per-user fee. A team of 10 on Time Premium pays $120 a month, and a team of 25 pays $270.


**Best for:** Businesses already on QuickBooks Online.


**Rating:**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/quickbooks-time/reviews) 4.5 ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/151722/TSheets/reviews/) 4.7


**What it is:** A time clock app from Intuit, formerly TSheets, with scheduling, alerts, and a time kiosk. Details are on the[QuickBooks Time](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/time-tracking/#nofollow) site.


**Key capabilities:**


- Workforce app for clock-in, with photo attachments.
- Time kiosk for a shared device.
- Alerts, notifications, and time off.
- Payroll and invoicing sync.
- Mileage, projects, estimates versus actuals, and timesheet signatures on Elite.


**Pricing:** Time Premium is $20 per month plus $10 per user, and Time Elite is $40 plus $12 per user. The base fee covers one admin, and a QuickBooks Online account is required. There’s no free plan.


**What users like:** “The GPS check-in feature saves us a lot of time,” writes a finance manager on[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/151722/TSheets/reviews/) .


**What users criticize:** A bookkeeper on Capterra says the GPS tracking has a catch:[“employees can simply turn off location services after clocking in.”](https://www.capterra.com/p/151722/TSheets/reviews/)


**Our take:** Check the geofencing line before you buy. It appears under the Workforce Elite bundle on QuickBooks’ plan page, not under standalone Time Elite. The base fee also stings small teams most: at five employees on Premium, you’re paying $14 per person.


### **5. Deputy: time and attendance software for multi-location shifts.**


Deputy pairs a time clock with scheduling, shift swaps, and leave, which suits teams juggling several rosters. The headline price is $5.50 per user per month on Lite, but biometric clocking and timesheet auto approval start on Core at $7.25. Monthly plans also carry a $30 minimum.


**Best for:** Teams with several areas or locations and complex shifts.


**Rating:**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/deputy/reviews) 4.5 ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/167811/Deputy/reviews/) 4.6


**What it is:** A workforce management app for shift-based teams, with the time clock built into the roster. Plans are listed on the[Deputy](https://deputy.com/#nofollow) site.


**Key capabilities:**


- Basic time clocking and timesheets on Lite.
- Biometric time clocking and timesheet auto approval on Core.
- Shift swaps, leave, and availability management.
- Demand forecasting and auto-scheduling on Core and Pro.
- Custom access levels and advanced timesheets on Pro.


**Pricing:** Lite is $5.50, Core is $7.25, and Pro is $10 per user per month, with a $30 minimum monthly spend. There’s no free plan.


**What users like:** A practice manager at a multi-site organization calls it a[“fast, efficient way to complete rosters, timesheets”](https://www.g2.com/products/deputy/reviews) and more.


**What users criticize:** A manager at a large employer on G2 reports[“WAY too many notifications about someone coming in a few minutes late.”](https://www.g2.com/products/deputy/reviews)


**Our take:** Deputy works best when scheduling is the main job and the time clock comes with it. If your team mostly needs accurate clock-ins, you’re paying for roster tools you may not use. Tune the late alerts so managers don’t tune them out.


### **6. When I Work: employee time clock app for shift-based teams.**


When I Work starts with the schedule and adds a time clock you switch on for each plan, with GPS or geofenced clock-in. Plans start at $2.50 per user per month, and there’s no free plan beyond a 14-day trial.


**Best for:** Shift teams that start from scheduling.


**Rating:**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/when-i-work/reviews) 4.4 ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/121248/When-I-Work/reviews/) 4.5


**What it is:** A scheduling app with an optional time clock and team messaging. Pricing is on the[When I Work](https://wheniwork.com/#nofollow) site.


**Key capabilities:**


- GPS or geofenced clock-in when time tracking is switched on.
- Overtime and paid break tracking.
- Shift swaps, open shifts, and shift confirmation alerts.
- Payroll and POS integrations.


**Pricing:** Essentials is $2.50, Pro is $5, and Premium is $8 per user per month, with Time Tracking & Attendance added by a toggle on each plan. There’s no free plan, and a 14-day free trial is available.


**What users like:** A reviewer on[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/121248/When-I-Work/reviews/?page=4) calls it an “easy clock-in kiosk” that’s simple for the team to learn.


**What users criticize:** A salon director on G2 writes,[“I wish it would allow us to add the 10-minute paid breaks,”](https://www.g2.com/products/when-i-work/reviews) the way it does for 30-minute unpaid lunches. A retail owner on[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/121248/When-I-Work/reviews/?page=12) adds that time cards can’t be approved for a manager who’s scheduled but not required to clock in.


**Our take:** Strong value for scheduling-first teams. The gaps show up in the details of hourly pay, like paid breaks and approvals for managers who don’t clock in.


### **7. Time Clock Wizard: time clock software for small business on a flat rate.**


Time Clock Wizard prices by plan instead of by person: Value is $34.95 a month for unlimited users, and Pro starts at $54.95 for up to 50. At 25 employees, Value costs a fraction of QuickBooks Time’s $270. The tradeoff, according to reviewers, is occasional trouble connecting at clock-in.


**Best for:** Teams that prefer flat-rate pricing to per-user pricing.


**Rating:**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/time-clock-wizard/reviews) 4.6 ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/154850/Time-Clock-Wizard/reviews/) 4.4


**What it is:** A web-based time clock and hourly work tracker with a free plan, plus iOS and Android apps on paid plans. Plans are listed on the[Time Clock Wizard](https://www.timeclockwizard.com/#nofollow) site.


**Key capabilities:**


- Free plan for unlimited users with basic time tracking.
- Pro adds scheduling, payroll reporting, and a GPS employee locator.
- Mobile apps for iOS and Android on paid plans.
- Phone, chat, and email support.


**Pricing:** Free for unlimited users with basic tracking. Value is $34.95, Pro starts at $54.95 for up to 50 users, and Enterprise is $249.95 per month.


**What users like:** One[Capterra reviewer](https://www.capterra.com/p/154850/Time-Clock-Wizard/reviews/) praises “easy adjustments to time if you forget to clock in and out.”


**What users criticize:** A business systems analyst in construction writes that[“sometimes it does not connect and does not let users clock in or out.”](https://www.capterra.com/p/154850/Time-Clock-Wizard/#Capterra___7125620)


**Our take:** Flat pricing is the draw, and it wins at 25 or more users. Before you commit, test clock-in at your weakest Wi-Fi spot, since connection trouble is the complaint to check.


## **What to Look for in Hourly Employee Time Tracking Software**


The right hourly employee time tracking software handles the messy parts of an hourly week: early arrivals, skipped breaks, missed punches, and overtime that sneaks up. Five things separate the apps that hold up from the ones that create more work.


**What’s the best time tracker for employees?** The best time tracking app for employees is the one your team uses every shift. For hourly teams, that means a fast clock-in on a phone or shared tablet, overtime alerts, easy punch fixes, and clean hours in payroll. Price it at your real headcount, not the headline per-user rate.


### **GPS time clock app and geofencing for hourly teams.**


GPS stamps record where a phone was at clock-in. Geofencing goes further and blocks or flags a punch made outside the radius you set.


Owners in one[r/TimeTrackingSoftware thread](https://www.reddit.com/r/TimeTrackingSoftware/comments/1v2y73k/whats_the_best_employee_time_clock_app_for/) about stopping clock-ins from home kept landing on the same advice:


- Geofencing is the capability to look for.
- Test it at the edge of each site.
- Test it in weak signal.
- Test it with the least tech-comfortable person on the team.


Many replies in that thread come from vendors, so weigh them accordingly.


GPS is a paid capability on most apps:


- Essentials on Homebase.
- Pro on Clockify.
- Included free on Jibble.


A shared tablet with PINs and photo capture can be enough when everyone works at one counter. For notice and consent rules, see our guide to the[best small business time clocks](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/best-small-business-time-clock) , and our explainer on the[GPS time clock app](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/gps-time-clock-app) .


### **Overtime tracking software and break alerts for hourly pay.**


Picture a team member scheduled for 38 hours who picks up a three-hour Saturday shift. The week reads 41. Under federal overtime rules, hours past 40 in a workweek generally pay at time and a half, so that last hour costs $25.14 instead of $16.76, the average hourly wage across Homebase payroll customers. State rules can be stricter, as our guide to[overtime laws by state](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/overtime-laws-by-state) explains.


Overtime tracking software alerts you at 38 or 39 hours, while there’s still time to swap the shift.


Break alerts do the same job for meal and rest periods:


- A skipped break flagged at 2pm is a fix.
- A skipped break found on payday is a problem you can’t undo.


Overtime tools vary by app:


- **Homebase:** alerts when employees approach or reach overtime.
- **Clockify:** an attendance and overtime report on Standard and up.


### **Buddy punching prevention with PIN and photo capture.**


Buddy punching is when one employee clocks in for another. Three layers close the gap:


1. **PIN:** puts a name on every punch.
2. **Photo capture or face recognition:** shows who’s standing there.
3. **Location check:** shows where.


On a shared tablet, PINs plus photos stop most of it. On phones, location checks do the same work.


Our guide to[buddy punching](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/buddy-punching) covers the warning signs.


### **Timesheet approvals and edit history in a clock in clock out app.**


Every team forgets a punch. What matters is the fix:


1. The employee flags it.
2. The manager approves it.
3. The app records who changed what and when.


Look for these in any app:


- Approval workflows (Clockify starts them on Standard, Deputy adds auto approval on Core).
- An edit history on each time card.
- Time approval for managers who don’t clock in, the gap one When I Work reviewer ran into.


Our[timesheets](https://www.joinhomebase.com/timesheets) show edit history, waived breaks, and overtime on location-verified time cards, which makes a time card app for employees easier to defend if a pay question comes up.


### **Payroll time tracking software and scheduling hand-off.**


Hours should reach payroll without retyping, and time tracking software with payroll built in skips the step entirely. Here’s how each app gets them there:


- **QuickBooks Time:** syncs to QuickBooks.
- **Deputy:** adds payroll through Paycor on annual Core and Pro plans.
- **Homebase:**[syncs hours with QuickBooks Online Plus, Gusto, and ADP RUN](https://www.joinhomebase.com/integrations) , exports timesheets formatted for Paychex, or runs payroll itself through its[payroll](https://www.joinhomebase.com/payroll) add-on.


For a wider look, see our guide to[time and attendance software](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/time-and-attendance-software) .


Recordkeeping matters here too. The U.S. Department of Labor sets these minimums:


- Payroll records: at least three years.
- Time cards: at least two years.


The[full requirements](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/21-flsa-recordkeeping) are in DOL Fact Sheet #21, and some states require longer.

- **Kiosk:** Clockify’s shared-device kiosk starts on a paid plan.

## **How Much Time Theft Costs a Small Hourly Team**


Time theft sounds dramatic, but it usually looks small: a few minutes added to a punch, a coworker who clocks in for a friend. Good hourly employee time tracking software closes most of those gaps, and the math shows how fast they add up.


### **Time theft by the numbers for a 10-person team.**


According to the[Homebase Main Street Health Report](https://www.joinhomebase.com/data/september-2026-main-street-health-report) , the average hourly wage across Homebase payroll customers is $16.76. Here’s the cost of 10 minutes a day per employee:


- 10 minutes a day × 5 days × 52 weeks is about 43.3 hours per employee per year.
- At $16.76 an hour, that’s about $726 per employee, or about **$7,260 for a team of 10** .
- At the Food and Drink average of $14.24, it’s about $6,170. At the Retail average of $16.03, it’s about $6,945.


## **How to Roll Out Time Tracking for Hourly Employees**


Even the best hourly employee time tracking software only works if your team uses it. That goes for any hourly tracker app, free or paid, so a short rollout plan makes adoption far more likely.


### **Test an employee clock in app for one week first.**


Before you commit, run a one-week test, or one pay period side by side with your current method, the approach owners in that Reddit thread suggested. Test GPS at the edge of your site and in weak signal, fix a missed punch, and look at the hours export your bookkeeper will receive. Our guide to[how to track employee hours](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/how-to-track-employee-hours) covers the full setup.


### **Answering pushback when you roll out time tracking for hourly employees.**


Expect “you don’t trust us.” The honest answer is that accurate records protect employees and owners both, especially when a pay question comes up. Tell your team exactly what’s tracked, such as location at clock-in, clock-out, and breaks only, and put it in writing with our[attendance policy template](https://www.joinhomebase.com/tools/attendance-policy-template) . At Active Education, clock-in notifications tell the director when someone is running late across 40 to 55 remote employees, so problems surface the same day.


## **Choosing the Right Hourly Employee Time Tracking Software**


The right hourly employee time tracking software matches how your team clocks in, costs what you expect at your real headcount, and produces records you can stand behind. Three checks get you there: match the clock-in method to your floor, price the app at 10 or 25 employees, and keep time cards for at least two years and payroll records for three.


If hours live in one tool, schedules in another, and payroll in a third, one login ends the juggling. Start with the[Homebase time clock](https://www.joinhomebase.com/free-time-clock) , free with no credit card required, and add[Homebase payroll](https://www.joinhomebase.com/payroll) when you’re ready.


## **Hourly Employee Time Tracking Software FAQs**


### **What is the best time tracker for employees?**


The best time tracker for employees fits how your team clocks in and what you can pay at your real headcount. For hourly teams at one or a few locations, Homebase pairs a free time clock with scheduling and payroll.


Clockify and Jibble are strong free options for the smallest teams.


### **Is there a free employee time tracking app to track work hours?**


Several free employee time tracking apps track work hours, and the limits differ. The free plan from Homebase covers one location and up to 10 employees, Clockify is free for up to five users, and Jibble is free for unlimited users.


Check each plan’s GPS and export limits before you commit.


### **How to track employee hours?**


Track employee hours by having every employee clock in on a phone or shared tablet, then review timesheets before each payroll run. Set overtime alerts so you see long weeks before they end, and keep an edit history for every change.


Our guide to[tracking employee hours](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/how-to-track-employee-hours) walks through the full setup.


### **Is time tracking for hourly employees legal?**


Time tracking for hourly employees is legal and generally required for non-exempt employees under federal law. Employers are expected to keep accurate records of the hours worked.


Some states regulate biometric data and location tracking, so check your state’s requirements in our[state labor law guides](https://www.joinhomebase.com/state-labor-laws) .


### **How long do I need to keep time cards from an employee time clock app?**


Time cards from an employee time clock app follow the same federal rule as paper ones: keep them for at least two years, and payroll records for at least three. Some states require longer, so check your state’s rules.


Digital timesheets make this easier, because the records are stored and searchable instead of sitting in a drawer.


### **What is hourly employee time tracking software?**


Hourly employee time tracking software records when each hourly employee starts and stops work, then turns those punches into timesheets for payroll. Most apps add overtime alerts, break tracking, approvals, and GPS or photo checks.


The best ones also connect to scheduling and payroll, so hours move on their own.


### **Can employees use their own phones for a time clock app with GPS?**


Employees can use their own phones with any time clock app with GPS that offers a mobile clock-in. Most also support a shared tablet or computer at the counter for teams that prefer not to use personal devices.


Our[mobile time clock](https://www.joinhomebase.com/time-clock/mobile-time-clock) works on phones, tablets, computers, and POS devices.


### **How does a geofence time clock stop employees from clocking in from home?**


A geofence time clock stops clock-ins from home by blocking or flagging a punch made outside the radius you set around your site. Set the radius wide enough to cover parking, and test it at the edge of the property.


Review flagged punches, because phone location can drift in weak signal.
